findings.summary: Documents attributed to different authors share distinctive, non-slogan sentences near-verbatim, so a cross-document read exposes one generator hand behind supposedly independent writers.
findings.evidence: The kickoff memo d:0023 (from John Sanchez) and the kickoff memo d:0030 (from William Schwartz) both carry the identical clause 'with no one left to ask what a note meant', each followed by 'So we write the record ... [we make it legible without us / so it reads without us]', and each closes with 'the first day on site is spent [sampling/measuring] and not deciding.' The tell crosses into client-facing prose too: 'You will not have to chase us for status' appears verbatim in d:0022 (engagement letter, Flynn) and d:0032 (status report, Schwartz). These are literary turns, not firm slogans, so two fresh writers would not land on them independently.
